title: Conversation-gated workflow ideas for adaptive fidelity
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight personal sketch for a feature I keep sketching in meetings: a conversation-gated workflow system that lets product teams define rules and UI hooks for changing inference fidelity, routing, and tool usage based on signals observed in the session.

Why (problem):
- Customers want predictable costs and quality but many prod apps need to change model behavior inside a single conversation (e.g., escalate model quality when user asks for a contract, reduce quality for short chitchat).
- Right now teams either: ship conservative high-cost configs everywhere, or build brittle app-side heuristics.
- We could offer a first-class, composable way to declare gates and transitions tied to session signals (intent, token budget, time, user role, sticky flags).

High-level idea:
- A gate is a named rule bundle evaluated against the live session. Gates can trigger: model upgrade/downgrade, enable/disable tool calling, change temperature/top-p, switch to cached response, or route to an enterprise-only path.
- Hooks expose gate state to client SDKs and Console so UX can show transitional states (e.g., "entering high-fidelity mode").
- Policy ordering + fallback chain: each session maintains an ordered pipeline of gates; first match wins with optional canary and fallback behaviors.

Primary personas:
- Product engineer building a chat-based legal assistant: wants automatic fidelity bump when user mentions legal terms or uploads attachments requiring careful wording.
- Platform/infra owner: wants predictable unit economics and easy rollout of gating rules with observability.
- SRE/ops: wants safe defaults and circuit-breakers (avoid sudden capex spikes).

Success metrics (initial):
- Reduction in average cost-per-session for targeted flows by >= 12% within 30 days of enabling gating on non-critical paths.
- Fraction of high-risk queries that see fidelity upgrade when gate condition present >= 95%.
- No increase in user-facing latency > 10th percentile SLA threshold; goal: latency impact < 5%.

User stories / rough acceptance criteria:
1) As a product engineer, I can declare a gate that upgrades model from m-base to m-high when message contains taxonomy keywords and user has "paid" flag.
   - Accept: gate rule UI/JSON can express keyword match + user attribute + count thresholds.
   - Accept: when rule matches, subsequent generation calls in that session use m-high.

2) As a platform owner, I can add a throttled budget gate that stops upgrades when dedicated capacity above 80% (soft-fail to fallback model).
   - Accept: gate can reference system signal (capacity metric) and define fallback target.

3) As an engineer, I can expose gate state to the client SDK so UI can show "High fidelity enabled" banner.
   - Accept: SDK receives ephemeral session metadata header with active gates (names + TTL).

4) As an SRE, I can roll out a new gate via canary (5% sessions) and see per-gate metrics (cost, success rate, latency).
   - Accept: Console shows gate-level metrics and allow promotion to 100%.

API / config sketch (informal):
- Gate definition (YAML/JSON):
  name: "legal-fidelity-upgrade"
  triggers:
    - type: message_keyword
      keywords: [contract, agreement, clause, liability]
      min_matches: 1
    - type: user_attribute
      attribute: subscription
      value: paid
  actions:
    - type: model_switch
      target: m-high-v2
    - type: ui_flag
      flag: fidelity_banner
  rollout: {percent: 5, canary: true}
  budget_guard: {metric: dedicated_gpu_util, threshold: 0.8, fallback: m-base-quant}

- Runtime: gates are evaluated at message boundary before generation. Evaluation returns gate decisions + reason codes. Decisions are cached per-session with TTL to avoid re-evaluating every token.

Console UX notes (quick):
- Gate list page: name, triggers summary, active % rollout, recent matches/time-series.
- Per-gate sample matches table (redact sensitive content).
- Quick toggle to force-enable for a session id for debugging.

Observability / telemetry:
- Emit events: gate_evaluated (session, gate, matched?, decision, reason, triggered_action, cost_delta_estimate).
- Per-gate dashboards: match rate, upgrade rate, avg latency delta, cost delta, rollback triggers.

Safety and guardrails:
- Require admin permission for gates that route to private models or enterprise paths.
- Budget guard default: fallback to cheaper quantized model when utilization high.
- Rate-limit model upgrades per-session (no more than 2 upgrades per 24h) to avoid billing surprises.

Rollout plan (MVP):
- Phase 0 (prototype, 2 weeks): implement gate eval library + local SDK flagging; PoC rule for keyword match -> model switch; smoke tests.
- Phase 1 (1 month): server-side gate store + simple Console list, telemetry pipeline; 5% canary traffic for one customer internal.
- Phase 2 (2 months): expose rollout controls, capacity guard integration, SDK UX hooks, per-gate dashboards.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How to handle multi-gate conflicts (priority vs. merge actions)? Simple ordered priority for MVP, but consider composable effects later.
- TTL: how long should gate decisions persist for an idle session? 5–30 minutes? tradeoffs: re-eval cost vs. stale decisions.
- Security/PII: gate triggers that use message content need clear retention and redaction policies.
- Billing transparency: surface estimated cost delta in Console before enabling gate at 100%.

Next steps (short):
- Share sketch with Noah + Maya, ask for quick feasibility call (15–30m).
- Draft minimal gate proto and telemetry schema in routing-proto repo (link above).
- Run through console mockups with PM to validate rollout UX.

Notes to self (todo):
- Add sample user stories with edge cases (attachments, multi-turn references).
- Think through SDK-level caching contract and server TTL.
- Check legal on sample redaction policy for per-gate match logs.

---
Small personal log: initial thought came from Jamie's latency investigation meeting where we noticed many search-chit-chat sessions that never need high-fidelity answers. A gating system could lower costs without fragile app-level hacks.
